solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A clockwork egg

parts.note: egg is old service slang for a bomb or mine, and a bomb run by a clock mechanism is set to go off at a fixed moment

explanation.surface: A wind-up toy egg, the kind of novelty found in a nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg' reads as a toy or something for breakfast, but in slang it is a bomb; one worked by clockwork detonates on a timer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a device triggered by a timing mechanism, with egg as slang for an explosive.

clue.text: Carried baby Edward

parts.note: a tot is a small child
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Little Edward was carried around.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to tote something is to lug or haul it about.

clue.text: Symbolically represent most of defect in middle of Yemen

indicators.note: in puts the trimmed flaw inside the central letters of the country
the middle of a word is what remains once its first and last letters are removed
most of says nearly all the word is kept, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a blemish is a defect or flaw

explanation.surface: Using a flaw at the heart of Yemen to stand for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' drops the first and last letters of Yemen; 'most of' drops the final letter of the flaw before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make something an emblem of an idea is to represent it in symbols.

clue.text: Company has a bit of Inverness kale prepared for cattle food

indicators.note: prepared as food is prepared, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement
a bit of a word is only a small piece, here its opening letter

explanation.surface: A firm uses some Highland kale to make fodder for cows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges CO, I and KALE together; Inverness is a city in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: compressed seed residue left after pressing out oil, fed to livestock.

clue.text: Idle pleasure at the Red Lion?

definitions.text: Idle pleasure at the Red Lion?

parts.words: Idle pleasure at the Red Lion?
parts.note: the Red Lion is a common English pub name; a pub offers drink and the old pub game of ninepins, and the phrase means carefree enjoyment

explanation.surface: Lazy enjoyment at the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Lion is a typical British pub name; skittles is a pub game like bowling. The phrase 'life is not all ...' means life is not all fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a byword for easy carefree amusement, literally the drink and ninepins of a pub.

clue.text: Matched, beheaded yet joined in some way

indicators.note: a beheaded word loses its head, so the first letter is cut off

parts.note: figures that matched have tallied, agreeing with each other

explanation.surface: Someone matched and executed, yet still somehow connected: a grim paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: nations or people bound together by a treaty or pact are joined in a particular way.

clue.text: Incidentally one gets support for Unix, say

parts.note: a means one
a prop is a support
Unix is an example of an OS, an operating system

explanation.surface: By the way, someone is backing the Unix computer system.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: used as an adverb, it means by the way, introducing a side remark.

clue.text: Lighter soldier blown up by nitre exploding

indicators.note: in a down clue, blown up means sent upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: exploding blows the letters apart so they land in a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier caught in a blast of nitre is a lighter man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' reads as a comparative adjective but is the noun: something that lights. 'blown up' turns the soldier over, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a device that sets fire to something, a lighter or detonator.

clue.text: Brand of cola in off days produces indigestion

indicators.note: in sets the cola brand inside the rearranged letters
off means not right, so the letters of the word are put in a wrong order

parts.note: Pepsi is a well-known cola brand

explanation.surface: Drinking a certain cola on bad days gives you an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges days to DYSA, with PEPSI inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the medical term for an upset stomach or difficulty digesting.

clue.text: A hint of bias in examination of a family group

indicators.note: in places the hinted letter inside the word for examination

parts.note: a trial is an examination, as in a court hearing or a test

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just a trace of it, so only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A slight prejudice shown while examining a family group.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIAL is examination in the courtroom sense, the hearing of a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective: something relating to a tribe, a kinship-based community, is described this way.

clue.text: Grannies making profits

indicators.note: making here means forming something new out of the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Old ladies turning a tidy profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: money earned or gained from work or investment counts as profits.

clue.text: Cocktail of rare mead, rum and sugar

indicators.note: a cocktail mixes its ingredients, so these letters are mixed up
rum in the old sense of odd or strange tells us the letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: A drink made of unusual mead, rum and sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Cocktail of' and 'rum' signal the mix; 'rum' is the adjective meaning odd, not the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a light brown cane sugar named after a region of Guyana.

clue.text: Troublesome insect on the French instrument

parts.note: a pest is an insect that causes trouble
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A bothersome bug landing on a French musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tool for pounding in a mortar is a kind of instrument, not a musical one.

clue.text: Women try to avoid this port at the finish

parts.note: Split is a port on the Croatian coast
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Women steering clear of a certain harbour at the end of a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a place to avoid visiting; it is a hair problem women try to prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a frayed tip of a hair is something many women take care to prevent.

clue.text: Idiot introduced to silly prudes excelled

indicators.note: introduced to means put into, so the fool goes inside the other letters
silly means foolish or messed up, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A fool is brought into a group of prim people and outshone them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced to' places the idiot after the fourth letter of the rearranged prudes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have gone beyond or outdone others is to have excelled.

clue.text: Fathers embrace positive features of the church

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: sires are fathers

explanation.surface: Priests hugging the hopeful aspects of church life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fathers' suggests priests in a church setting, but here it means sires.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: tall pointed towers are typical architectural parts of a church building.

clue.text: Use distinctive type to stress facilities left by France

indicators.note: stress taken as strain or pressure, so the letters are put under pressure and rearranged
left by means abandoned by, so the France letter departs from the word

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Using a special font to emphasise amenities that France has left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left by' removes F from facilities; 'stress' rearranges ACILITIES. 'Stress' also fits the definition, as slanted type gives emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: setting words in sloping print is using a distinctive typeface.

clue.text: Take letter in alcove

parts.note: REC is short for recipe, Latin for take, as written at the head of old prescriptions
ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: An instruction to collect a letter from a nook in the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Recipe, the Latin imperative 'take', is abbreviated REC as well as the usual R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a set-back space in a wall, a niche, is an alcove.

clue.text: Framework from vehicle on Central American ship

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
CA is the abbreviation for Central America
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A frame taken from a vehicle carried on a Central American ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the structural shell or skeleton of something, like a building's frame.

clue.text: Sounding so Sinatra's almost English

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Nancy Sinatra, the singer, is Frank's daughter

explanation.surface: Sinatra singing in almost English style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinatra' wants to be Frank; it is his daughter Nancy, trimmed by 'almost' to NANC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rare noun for the quality or condition of making sound.

clue.text: Politician leaves Takoma Park to reform island

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaves means goes away from, so the politician's letters are taken out

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician quits a Maryland town in order to reform an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes M and P out of TAKOMAPARK; 'to reform' rearranges the TAKOAARK left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a volcanic island in Indonesia famous for its huge 1883 eruption.

clue.text: Thrown as a dart, going like a rocket

indicators.note: thrown means tossed about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Hurled like a dart, it flies off like a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair as the Latin phrase means to the stars, where a rocket goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase meaning towards the stars, the direction of a launched rocket.

clue.text: Boy runs into a goddess

indicators.note: into places the runs letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: Dian is a poetic form of Diana, the Roman goddess of the hunt
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A boy dashes into a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: DIAN is the poetic short form of Diana, so 'a goddess' gives A DIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a male given name, so it serves as a boy in crosswords.

clue.text: Empresses beheaded partisans after revolution

indicators.note: after a revolution things are turned around, so the letters are reordered
beheaded means the word loses its head, its first letter

explanation.surface: Royal women who executed rebels once the uprising was over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' strips the P from partisans, leaving ARTISANS; 'after revolution' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the wives of Russian emperors were empresses.

clue.text: Utensil is upset by girl

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down clue reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool is knocked over by a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a mesh strainer used in the kitchen is a utensil.

clue.text: Timely introduction of a native to sea loch

indicators.note: introduction of means putting one thing into another, here the native and a into the sea loch

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake
a native son is someone born in a place, so native gives son

explanation.surface: Putting a local into a sea loch at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: A native son is one born in a place. The two pieces from 'a native' go in with the son before the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something suited to the time of year, coming at the right season, is timely.

clue.text: Amuse oneself in most of fertile ground

indicators.note: ground as in crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
most of means nearly all the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Enjoying oneself on a patch of rich farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims fertile to FERTIL; 'ground' rearranges it. 'Ground' looks like a noun for soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to play or toy idly with something is a way of amusing oneself.

clue.text: Longing to reside at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Yearning to live on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a strong wish or yearning for something is a longing.

clue.text: Cleanse archdeacon in special prison

indicators.note: in places the archdeacon's title inside the other pieces

parts.note: a cage is a slang word for a prison or a barred enclosure
an archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: Purifying a senior cleric held in a special jail.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is styled the Venerable. The cleansing sense is old, as of sweeping streets clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic sense: to clean dirt from streets, the origin of the scavenger as street sweeper.
